newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks retreat from highs to end steady.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks retreat from highs to end steady.

text.p: The Australian share market trod a wary path to a slightly firmer finish on Tuesday with one eye on Wall Street and a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting and the other on local annual corporate report cards.
The All Ordinaries index crept up 2.4 points to 2,620.9.

The market rebounded early as U.S. markets staged a comeback from Friday's sharp fall, but the weight of weaker metals prices hindered progress among the major miners which eventually dragged the benchmark index off its highs to the narrow finish.
"It's been a pretty average day," said one Sydney broker, noting the modest level of business and investor interest.
"There is no local news that has generated much interest -- it is all on the profit results at the moment."
Caution ahead of U.S. moves tonight came to the fore late with traders wary rather than fearful of another dramatic move.
"The U.S. Fed is meeting tonight and that will give us some more insight," said Hartley Poynton broker Justin Hondris.
"No-one is predicting any interest rate change there but if there is it will have an effect on us."

It was a busy day for profit results with the biggest being from newspaper publisher John Fairfax. Its shares ended one cent lower at A$3.18 (US$2.35) after a 15 percent lower year net profit of A$73.94 million.
Capral Aluminium shares added three cents to A$4.48 despite a slightly lower half-year net profit of A$17.8 million.
Among the leaders Rio Tinto and WMC failed to make any ground as metals prices pressured miners. Rio Tinto shares lost 17 cents to A$20.81, while WMC shed nine to A$7.19.
Among industrials, media giant News Corp finished three higher at A$5.95 ahead of its annual results, due Wednesday.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 25 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
